## Motivation

GLM-5.3-Flash has 34 KDA layers. On CUDA each of them runs three kernels per decode step: `causal_conv1d_update`, the recurrence, and the gated RMSNorm. Kimi-K3 runs the same step as one kernel (`kda_fused_decode`): its layers have the same head dim 128, conv width 4 and gate lower bound, but the kernel is only built for 3/6/12 heads per rank. GLM-5.3-Flash has 8 heads per rank at TP8 and 16 at TP4, which is what the cookbook's NVIDIA High Throughput recipes run (H100/H200/B200/B300 TP8, GB300 TP4, spec decode off).

Also, safe-gate layers never take packed decode on CUDA, because `TritonKDAKernel` doesn't declare `supports_packed_decode_safe_gate`, so the recurrence is the unpacked kernel.

Roadmap: #42473 (Kernels), GLM-5.3-Flash Hopper tracker #45373.

## Modifications

- `kda_fused_decode.cuh`: instantiate the fused decode kernel for 8 and 16 local heads, one CTA per (token, head). The arithmetic is unchanged; the only other kernel change is the SM90 state cache hints below.
- `kda_fused_decode.py`: `SUPPORTED_HEADS = {3, 6, 8, 12, 16}`. Kimi-K3 reads this set since #47526, so K3 at 8/16 heads per rank (TP12, TP6) also takes the fused kernel; it matches the unfused chain there with no lower bound on 1x H200.
- `glm5_next.py`: `Glm5NextLinearAttention._prepare_fused_decode()` runs from both `load_weights` and `post_load_weights` (dummy and other loaders call only the latter). It stashes the kernel's static inputs (per-segment fp32 conv taps, zero conv bias, fp32 o_norm weight) and rebuilds them in place on later loads, since captured graphs hold them. In decode, `forward()` hands the o_norm gate to the KDA backend the same way Kimi-K3 does; if the backend doesn't take it, the layer applies o_norm as before.
- The fused path is offered on SM9x and SM10x only (the kernel stages the state with TMA). On Hopper it is used below `2048 // local_heads` tokens per step. From 2048 (token, head) blocks the unfused packed chain streams the fp32 state faster on H200. B200 has no cap.
- `TritonKDAKernel.supports_packed_decode_safe_gate = is_cuda()`, and safe-gate layers stay on the Triton packed kernel instead of the CUDA row kernel, which is slower at 8-32 heads per rank. This is the fallback for Hopper large batches and for TP1/TP2 (64/32 heads).
- On SM90 at 8/16 heads and up to 1024 (token, head) blocks, the kernel loads the state with an L2 evict-first hint and stores it with streaming stores (bit-identical outputs).
- `weight_updater.py`: a module can set `_direct_weight_update_error`, which rejects `update_weights_from_tensor(load_format="direct")` before any write. The direct format skips `load_weights` and `post_load_weights`, so GLM sets it once the fused decode inputs are published. The default format and the disk and distributed updates go through `load_weights` and refresh the buffers in place.
- Tests: GLM-5.3-Flash kernel cases (TP8 H=8, TP4 H=16, lower bound -5, both staging paths) in `test_kda_fused_decode.py`, plus one weight-loading test on a small real `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (both hooks at SM80/90/100/120: SM9x and SM10x publish the inputs and a reload rewrites the graph-held buffers in place, the others prepare nothing), a safe-gate dispatch test in `test_kda_kernels.py`, and a CPU test that the direct format is rejected while the default one still loads. Commits after `6911d48513`, where the GSM8K and H200 kernel numbers below ran, only change tests and merge main.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K with `sgl-eval`, official FP8 checkpoint on 4x H200, TP4/EP4 (16 KDA heads per rank), BF16 KV, cookbook H200 flags plus `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64`, no MTP, 1319 questions, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 8192, 64 threads, so decode stays under the 128-token cap. This PR and main ran in one container, one server each:

| | correct / 1319 | score | right only here |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (`3d33971dea`) | 1283 | 97.27% | 7 |
| this PR (`6911d48513`) | 1284 | 97.35% | 8 |

The fused path really ran: a counter on `kda_fused_decode` saw 4896 graph-capture calls on this PR and 0 on main.

Those same two servers, median `gen throughput` over the decode log lines at 56-64 running requests: main 1795 tok/s (60 lines), this PR 1868 tok/s (61 lines). One server per arm and not interleaved, so this only shows no regression on real weights. The proxy tables below are the speed evidence.

The fused kernel keeps q/k/v in fp32 between the conv and the recurrence, so it is closer to an fp64 reference than main's chain. Max abs error against an fp64 torch reference on 1x H200, over H 8/16, B 1-256, 8 seeds (1640 runs). Weights and inputs are the checkpoint's: KDA layer 5 conv taps, A_log, dt_bias and o_norm weight, with rows and state dumped from the first six layers served on real prompts. "Extreme" is zero/tiny/large inputs, saturated gates and long decay chains. "Packed chain" is what Hopper runs from 2048 (token, head) blocks.

| inputs | main out | main state | fused out | fused state | packed chain out | packed chain state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| real | 7.31e-4 | 3.23e-4 | 2.44e-4 | 4.47e-8 | 6.56e-4 | 3.23e-4 |
| extreme | 3.19e-3 | 2.19e-2 | 1.89e-3 | 9.54e-7 | 2.81e-3 | 2.13e-2 |

Kernel level, one GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layer decode step at one rank, real checkpoint weights and dumped real inputs in the layer's production layout, cold state (each call touches more than 4x L2 of state), CUDA graph. Both sides run the real `Glm5NextLinearAttention.forward` and `KDAAttnBackend.forward_decode`.

|---|---|---|---|

**Attention DP8** (64 heads per rank, so the packed fallback):

| Concurrency | main | this PR | this PR + BV=8 on SM90 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.73 ms | 12.70 ms (-0.2%) | 12.67 ms (-0.5%) |
| 8 | 12.80 ms | 12.78 ms (-0.2%) | 12.75 ms (-0.4%) |
| 16 | 14.53 ms | 14.47 ms (-0.4%) | 14.47 ms (-0.4%) |
| 64 | 19.65 ms | 19.46 ms (-1.0%) | 19.28 ms (-1.9%) |
| 128 | 23.35 ms | 23.07 ms (-1.2%) | 22.83 ms (-2.2%) |

(main is the mean of two servers; the PR columns are one server each. Our local SM90 branch, which runs the same BV=8 packed path, gave the last column within 0.5% on two more servers.)

**BV=8 for the Triton packed kernel on SM90.** `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` launches with BV=32. BV only sets how many V rows one program updates, so BV=8 is bit-identical (output and state); it launches 4x the programs and keeps more state rows in flight. On H20 it takes 6-22% less time than BV=32 per layer (median 17%; 8, 16 and 64 heads, batch 1-256, cold L2). That is the last column above. It also moves the fused/packed crossover on H20. One layer's decode step (conv + recurrence + gated RMSNorm), cold L2, contiguous inputs like `test_kda_fused_decode.py`, us:

| Heads | Batch | main chain | packed chain, BV=32 | packed chain, BV=8 | fused |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1 | 13.73 | 13.22 | 11.79 | 10.43 |
| 8 | 8 | 16.61 | 15.01 | 14.21 | 11.15 |
| 8 | 32 | 29.15 | 25.26 | 21.89 | 21.57 |
| 8 | 64 | 45.62 | 39.44 | 33.34 | 33.97 |
| 8 | 128 | 74.13 | 66.26 | 56.21 | 58.10 |
| 8 | 256 | 129.76 | 118.58 | 100.26 | 104.78 |
| 16 | 64 | 74.34 | 65.86 | 55.86 | 58.78 |
| 16 | 128 | 128.11 | 117.65 | 99.95 | 105.38 |
| 16 | 256 | 245.50 | 222.13 | 188.08 | 201.81 |

On H20 the fused kernel beats the BV=32 chain at every size we measured, up to 4096 (token, head) blocks, so from 2048 blocks (8 heads × 256 tokens, 16 heads × 128 and up) the SM90 cap hands the step to a chain that is 10-13% slower here. With BV=8 the chain wins from about 512 blocks, by up to 7%. Our inputs are contiguous rather than the fused projection's strided rows, so the crossover in the real layout may sit a little differently.

**B300 (SM103, 148 SMs).** The same BV question applies to SM10x, where this PR also falls back to the Triton packed kernel at 32 and 64 heads per rank (TP2, TP1 and attention DP). One layer's decode state update with the safe gate, CUPTI device time, state read from HBM, glm5_next's strided inputs, us:

| Heads | Batch | Triton packed, BV=32 | Triton packed, BV=8 | Change | CUDA row-streaming |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 1 | 5.3 | 4.5 | -16% | 14.8 |
| 32 | 32 | 29.7 | 26.5 | -11% | 37.6 |
| 32 | 256 | 192.4 | 171.9 | -11% | 212.8 |
| 64 | 1 | 5.8 | 5.1 | -13% | 15.3 |
| 64 | 16 | 29.7 | 26.6 | -10% | 37.9 |
| 64 | 128 | 193.8 | 174.6 | -10% | 212.6 |
| 64 | 256 | 380.7 | 339.0 | -11% | 412.1 |

Across 8-64 heads and batch 1-256, BV=8 takes 2-20% less time than BV=32 with the safe gate and 7-25% less without it, and its output and state are bit-identical to BV=32 at every shape. The row-streaming kernel is slower than the Triton kernel at every shape from batch 8 on this GPU too, with and without the safe gate, so B300 agrees with your H200/B200 finding for safe-gate layers.

End to end on 8×B300 with attention DP8 (64 heads per rank, so the packed fallback): this PR's head 6911d48513 merged onto main c0c7af402b, GLM-5.3-Flash FP8, the cookbook flags (TRT-LLM DSA, FP8 KV cache, `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE), no MTP, `--disable-radix-cache`, 1024-token random prompts, 256-512 output tokens, median ITL:

| Concurrency | main | this PR (2 servers) | this PR + BV=8 on SM10x (2 servers) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9.14 ms | 9.19 / 9.18 ms | 8.92 / 8.98 ms |
| 8 | 9.88 ms | 10.04 / 9.85 ms | 9.68 / 9.86 ms |
| 16 | 9.93 ms | 9.55 / 9.94 ms | 9.96 / 9.90 ms |
| 64 | 10.96 ms | 10.93 / 10.91 ms | 10.79 / 10.81 ms |
| 128 | 12.80 ms | 12.69 / 12.68 ms | 12.50 / 12.54 ms |
| 256 | 15.63 ms | 15.37 / 15.31 ms | 15.13 / 16.61 ms |

Servers of the same build differ by up to 4% at a given concurrency here, and at 256 concurrent an occasional server reads about 16.6-16.9 ms (one main server did too in an earlier run), so the profile is the cleaner signal. On the busy DP rank (one request, 34 layers), the recurrence takes 281 us per step on main, 183 us with this PR (BV=32) and 139 us with BV=8; the gated RMSNorm after it drops from 242 to 84 us with either. The greedy outputs with and without BV=8 are identical on three repeated requests, and GSM8K is 0.929 / 0.923 (one server each, all 1,319 questions).

This PR's tests also pass on B300 (`test_kda_fused_decode.py`, `test_kda_kernels.py` and the KDA/GDN unit tests: 47 passed, 1 skipped), apart from `TestKDAVerifyDecodeParity.test_bf16_state_verify_matches_single_token_launches` and `test_fp32_state_pool_is_not_rounded`, which fail the same way on main on this GPU.

Would you take BV=8 on SM90 and SM10x into this PR? It is two lines in `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode`. If you'd rather keep the PR as is, we can send it as a follow-up once this lands, and re-check the SM90 cap with it then.
